---
title: "Welcome"
---

These notes are a **draft course** on large language models (LLMs).
The first half is conceptual. The second half is practical: the same
ideas in Python, then in R, then a side-by-side comparison.

The book layout follows the Quarto **book** pattern used in
[BAUDOTlab/teaching_material](https://github.com/BAUDOTlab/teaching_material)
(HTML site plus a downloadable PDF).

## How to read this book {#sec-how-to-read}

1. **Theory.** Tokens, next-token prediction, and why models
   hallucinate ([LLM basics](theory/llm-basics.qmd)). Then three
   patterns that are often confused: MCP, RAG, and agents
   ([Tools versus agents](theory/tools-vs-agents.qmd)).
2. **Hosted tools.** ChatGPT companions, a short GPT shortlist, and
   `$` skills
   ([Pre-existing AI tools](tools/chatgpt-companions.qmd)).
3. **Python.** Tool calling, a minimal MCP server, then
   [tabular foundation models](python/tabular-foundation-models.qmd).
4. **R.** A condensed `ellmer` workshop, adapted from Hadley Wickham's
   [A no bullshit guide to LLMs](https://tidydesign.substack.com/p/a-no-bullshit-guide-to-llms)
   (useR! 2025 / Tidy Design, 2026), then R versus Python.

Live API calls are **not** evaluated at render time. Copy the chunks
into your own session after you have set a provider key.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-course-pipeline
%%| fig-cap: "Course pipeline: theory, hosted tools, then two implementation tracks."
%%{init: {'theme': 'sandstone'}}%%
flowchart TD
  T["Theory: how LLMs work"] --> P["Patterns: RAG, MCP, agents"]
  P --> H["Hosted tools: GPTs and skills"]
```

## Build locally {#sec-build}

From the repository root:

```bash
quarto render          # HTML and PDF under docs/; refreshes _freeze/
quarto preview         # live HTML preview
```

Requirements: [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) 1.8 or newer, plus a LaTeX
engine (`tinytex` or TeX Live) for the PDF. Executable chapters are
frozen locally (`_freeze/`, committed) so CI does not install `uv` or
`renv`. Lab scripts themselves: `uv sync` and `renv::restore()` on
your machine only.

## Repository map {#sec-map}

```text
.
├── theory/                 # conceptual chapters
├── tools/                  # hosted ChatGPT / GPT Store
├── config/
│   ├── skills/             # e.g. $maths-dollar
│   └── prompts/            # reusable system prompts
├── python/
│   ├── llm-tool-calling/   # lab: provider SDK + tools
│   └── basic-mcp-server/   # lab: tiny MCP server
├── R/
│   └── llm-integration/    # lab: ellmer scripts
├── figures/                # shared images
├── _freeze/                # local computation cache (commit this)
└── docs/                   # rendered HTML and PDF (gitignored)
```
